page: Amazon Web Services r8idb.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel processors running at 3.9 GHz under the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory is configured at 768.0 GB, providing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation that serves large working sets without utilizing hardware accelerators.

The instance includes 5,700 GB of local NVMe SSD storage directly attached to the host, facilitating high IOPS and low-latency storage access for temporary files, caching, and scratch spaces. Network performance is provisioned with a 100 Gbps baseline bandwidth, supporting high-throughput node synchronization and high-volume data ingest.

By bundling substantial local NVMe storage with high memory capacity, the server offers dense operational capability on a single node without requiring additional network-attached block storage for transient operations. Users must account for the ephemeral nature of instance store volumes to ensure data persistence across stop states. The hardware configuration matches requirements for in-memory databases, distributed key-value stores, relational database management systems, and memory-intensive ETL pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8idb.24xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a 3.9 GHz Intel x86_64 processor offering 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 48 physical cores with multithreading. Memory allocation is 768.0 GB, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio designed for memory-bound applications. The instance integrates 5,700 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage directly on the host, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. It contains no GPUs. By bundling significant local NVMe capacity with high-density RAM, r8idb.24xlarge delivers strong resource concentration for systems requiring low-latency storage I/O alongside large memory allocations. This profile is suited for production workloads such as in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, relational database hosting, and high-throughput real-time analytical processing pipelines.
